common.question: Does the rel="nofollow" attribute on a stylesheet-hidden canary link cause Qwen3-8B's lower follow rate on raw HTML, so that removing it from raw HTML raises the follow rate to within 10 points of markdown, and adding it to the markdown link lowers markdown to within 10 points of raw HTML?
common.gloss: (rel="nofollow": a tag in a link that asks search engines not to follow it. Canary link: a link people cannot see, so a visit marks an AI agent. Follow rate: the share of runs that opened it.)
common.page_note: A link in the page footer that people cannot see (the stylesheet hides it). It carries rel="nofollow", which asks search engines to skip it. Each run gets a new random address.
common.left_sub: the page as the server sends it
common.right_sub: same run: same site, task and random seed
common.row_mdhtml_sub: link written as an HTML <a> tag
common.md_no_tag: this link form has no place for the tag
common.key: Saw it: the link's random address was in what the tool returned. Opened: our server logged a visit to that address.

CONFIRMED.answer: Removing the tag lifted raw HTML from {raw} to {rawnf} of {n} runs (plain markdown: {md}). Adding it to markdown cut {mdhtml} to {mdnf} (raw HTML: {raw}).

REJECTED.answer: Without the tag, raw HTML still got only {rawnf} of {n} runs, against {md} for plain markdown. With the tag, markdown still got {mdnf} of {n}, against {raw} for raw HTML.

UNCONFIRMED_raw_only.answer: Removing the tag lifted raw HTML from {raw} to {rawnf} of {n} runs. But adding it to markdown left {mdnf} of {n} (without it: {mdhtml}). A Yes needed both.

UNCONFIRMED_md_only.answer: Adding the tag cut markdown from {mdhtml} to {mdnf} of {n} runs. But removing it from raw HTML left {rawnf} of {n} (with it: {raw}). A Yes needed both.

UNCONFIRMED_gate_gap.answer: This time raw HTML ({raw} of {n}) and plain markdown ({md}) were less than 10 points apart, so there was no gap for the tag to explain.
